newsitem.title: CANADA: No delay on Sable Island gas hearings, panel rules.
newsitem.headline: No delay on Sable Island gas hearings, panel rules.

text.p: Regulatory hearings on the proposed development of Sable Island gas fields and the Maritimes & Northeast pipeline will start as scheduled in April, a regulatory panel ruled on Monday.

The panel from Canada's National Energy Board rejected a request by the rival Trans Quebec & Maritimes (TQM) pipeline that the hearings be adjourned until its formal application could be submitted, spokesman Edward Sampson said.

Sampson said the panel will consider TQM's request for a delay in the final decision at the close of the hearings in May and will hear arguments during the hearings about TQM's preliminary application.
The hearings are scheduled to begin April 7 in Halifax and continue until May 30 with half the sessions held in Fredericton, New Brunswick.
The Sable Offshore Energy Project is owned primarily by Mobil Oil Canada, and has said that the Maritimes & Northeast project is its preferred pipeline route.
Trans Quebec & Maritimes is owned by TransCanada PipeLines Ltd and Gaz Metropolitain and Co LP. Maritimes & Northeast Pipeline, owned by Mobil, Westcoast Energy Inc and PanEnergy Corp.

Maritimes & Northeast would move the estimated 480 million cubic feet of gas per day to Northeast U.S. markets from Nova Scotia through New Brunswick and Maine. The TQM expansion would also move the gas to Boston, but via Quebec.
Maritimes & Northeast officials had charged that TQM submitted its proposal at the last minute as a delaying tactic and warned that any delay would sink the entire Sable Island project.

TQM submitted its preliminary application on March 7 and said that it would give the Energy Board a formal application in August. Backers of Sable Island want the board to rule on the project and preferred pipeline route by September.
